row.evidence: Firebase's IAM docs say project members are Google accounts, service accounts or Google groups assigned roles in the console or via Google Cloud IAM; no SCIM endpoint appears on the pricing page, in the docs sitemap or the IAM/API docs.
row.notes: Usage-priced (Spark no-cost, Blaze pay as you go), no per-seat plans, so per-user fields stay null. Console access is via Google accounts; project membership is managed through Google Cloud IAM (console or Resource Manager projects.setIamPolicy), so workforce provisioning happens upstream in Google Workspace/Cloud Identity rather than in Firebase. Granting Google groups lets group membership drive access. Firebase Authentication's SAML/OIDC MAUs on the pricing page are end-user auth for customers' apps, not workforce SSO. Okta's OIN 'Firebase' app is SWA only. Cloud Audit Logs record Firebase Management admin activity.

scim.notes: No SCIM in the Firebase docs sitemap (30,194 URLs, none matching 'scim'), pricing page or IAM docs.

user_api.notes: Project membership is an IAM policy on the Google Cloud project; there is no Firebase-specific member API.

capabilities.notes: Roles are granted/revoked to Google accounts, service accounts and Google groups by replacing the project IAM policy; Owner cannot be granted via setIamPolicy.

endpoints.purpose: Replace the project IAM policy (grant or remove member roles)

audit_log_api.notes: Via Google Cloud Audit Logs (Cloud Logging), service firebase.googleapis.com.

limitations.text: Owner role cannot be granted through setIamPolicy; the user must be invited in the console and accept.
setIamPolicy replaces the whole policy rather than appending.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SWA only (no SAML, OIDC or SCIM).

google.notes: Firebase members are Google accounts and Google groups natively; no separate catalogue app.

fallbacks.other_sync: Access follows Google accounts and Google groups (Google Workspace / Cloud Identity) granted IAM roles on the project
